item.title: Troops have been patrolling D.C. for a year. Experts are worried about elections
item.description: As the National Guard deployment in Washington, D.C., hits the one year mark, experts worry about the potential for President Trump to deploy the military during the upcoming election.
item.content:encoded: As the National Guard deployment in Washington, D.C., hits the one year mark, experts worry about the potential for President Trump to deploy the military during the upcoming election.
item.dc:creator: Kat Lonsdorf

item.title: A nonprofit helps thousands of musicians in Austin pay for insurance
item.description: Austin is lauded for its live music scene, but many musicians struggle to get by. A nonprofit helps thousands of them pay their monthly insurance premiums. And the model is being tried elsewhere.
item.content:encoded: Austin is lauded for its live music scene, but many musicians struggle to get by. A nonprofit helps thousands of them pay their monthly insurance premiums. And the model is being tried elsewhere.

item.title: The West's wildfire season is already breaking records, and it's not over
item.description: It's shaping up to be a historic wildfire season in the Western U.S. In Oregon, more acres have already burned than any time in modern history. At least 10 wildland firefighters have also died.
item.content:encoded: It's shaping up to be a historic wildfire season in the Western U.S. In Oregon, more acres have already burned than any time in modern history. At least 10 wildland firefighters have also died.

item.title: A judge expands a block on U.S. Postal Service work on Trump's mail-in voting order
item.description: A federal judge expanded a block on a key part of President Trump's order to restrict mail-in voting for this fall's midterms, banning the Postal Service from carrying out directives in every state.

item.title: In Spokane, those who lost homes to the fires are taking stock of the damage
item.description: Many of the people who lost their homes in the Spokane fires are just beginning to take stock of the damage and start to think about what it may look like to rebuild.

item.title: One Puerto Rico condo building. 10 families. No water
item.description: A drought is exposing weaknesses in the government's ability to deliver water. It's begun rationing. In one building in the capital, ten families have rearranged their lives around their faucets.

item.title: Kennedy Center must pay $250,000 in legal fees to musician who canceled in protest
item.description: Chuck Redd canceled his annual Christmas Eve performance to protest Trump's name being added to the complex. In June, a superior court judge dismissed the Kennedy Center's lawsuit against Redd.

item.title: In Minnesota and Wisconsin, competitive primaries will again test power of progressive candidates
item.description: A week after the Michigan primary, tests of progressive power will play out in the Midwest, raising questions of whether far left candidates can win come November or if the GOP can pick up moderates.

item.title: Alabama holds second primary Tuesday, leading to confusion, concerns about low turnout
item.description: After Alabama redrew its congressional maps in May, voters in several districts saw their primaries pushed to August. Now, it's time to vote and there are concerns confusion will dampen voter turnout.
